title: Building a Strong Identity: Key to an Impregnable Individuality
summary: A follow-up to NH's individuality video: identity is the mechanism that protects individuality, and it is built through time alone and self-analysis, then tested in social settings. Boundaries are the main tool for defending it, pictured as castle walls, an army and an emissary. Strong identities attract the right people and join collectives without dissolving into them.
claims: Identity is the mechanism that protects your individuality; without it individuality collapses at the first confrontation or manipulation
Pursuing any craft requires lots of time alone, which is torture if your self is empty
Many people and the world itself try to break down your individuality so they can use you like a puppet
Fitness has its own scam artists and bad influencers who try to replace your identity with theirs to take your money and attention
Everyone craves an identity; borrowing one from someone else is a Trojan horse they will use to their advantage
The strongest lifters, the ones who go furthest, have the strongest individualities
Most people know themselves only superficially and leave large parts of their personality unexplored
You should know yourself better than anyone; even his closest person knows him only about 60-70%, and keeping a secret garden is human, not dishonest
Psychoanalyze yourself whenever you can; becoming fluent in yourself is the most important language to learn
Self-exploration matters more than routines like 4 a.m. wake-ups, kale shakes or coffee enemas
Around others you mostly confirm what you already know about yourself; if others build your identity they hold shares in it and can break you
Personality is your identity projected outward, used to relate to others and to test the identity
Teenagers cycle through borrowed personalities to find what fits and what the group accepts; it's fine as refinement but harmful if you get stuck
Bullying either creates broken people or extremely tough ones, with little in between
Build the identity alone, then test it with others; never testing it means it has no value, like a boat never put to sea
Strong online personalities that melt down face to face reveal identities that were never strong
Boundaries are the most important tool for protecting identity; a boundary is only as strong as your commitment to it
In a non-violent society psychological attacks multiply because people can no longer punch you
Never let your boundaries fall: each breach teaches others and yourself that you are weak and weakens every future boundary
When forced to choose between protecting a boundary and upsetting someone, always protect the boundary
Castle metaphor: boundaries are walls, identity is the army, individuality is the treasure, personality is the emissary
A weak projected identity invites predators and repels strong people you would want to associate with
Being shy or introverted doesn't stop you having strong boundaries
You own your body and self; governments or corporations only control them if you allow it
Women often test men's boundaries not to change them but to see if they will cave; caving fails the test
Strong boundaries filter people: let in those who add to your treasure and respect your boundaries, cut those who get upset or keep negotiating
Weakness is not a state in which happiness can be reached
A strong identity lets you protect and shelter loved ones; you can't help others if you can't defend yourself
A healthy collective keeps each member's identity independent rather than melting them into a soup; collectives of weak identities are ruled by hidden tyrants or doomed
